spike_verdict: The spike (first lifeguard tower only in May 2018, five months after a father-son drowning) is clean and consistently sourced across surfaces. Two internal-consistency defects survive: the Honest Reckoning's drowning-count arithmetic contradicts its own itemized list, and the timeline array places a 2017 event before a 2014 event, breaking chronological order.

blocking.claim: "...could independently list at least six separate drowning deaths at Goat Rock Beach between 2003 and 2017: a 3-year-old girl in 2003, a kayaker in 2015, three people in 2016, and a father and his 6-year-old son in 2017. That is not a rounding error. It is a three-to-one gap..." / pullquote: "...local reporters could already document at least six."
blocking.problem: The note's own itemized list does not sum to six: 1 (2003 girl) + 1 (2015 kayaker) + 3 (2016) + 2 (2017 father and son) = 7 deaths, not 6. The stated total contradicts the list two sentences earlier, and the follow-on "three-to-one gap" (vs. NWS's reported 2) is then also off (7:2 is not 3:1). The pullquote repeats the same wrong total.
blocking.evidence: F35 (2003, 1 death), F34 (2015, 1 death), F33 (2016, three deaths), F32 (2017, father + son = 2 deaths) sum to 7, not 6.
blocking.fix: In honest_reckoning_note, change "could independently list at least six separate drowning deaths" to "could independently list at least seven separate drowning deaths", and change "It is a three-to-one gap" to "It is a gap of more than three to one". In reckoning_pullquote, change "local reporters could already document at least six." to "local reporters could already document at least seven."

blocking.claim: Array order: ...1985 (Goonies) -> 2003 (sneaker wave death) -> 2017-12 (father/son drown) -> 2014 (feasibility study) -> 2018-5 (lifeguard tower).
blocking.problem: The 2017-12 "Father and son drown off Goat Rock Beach" row is placed before the 2014 "Feasibility study weighs jetty's fate" row, out of chronological order. A reader scanning the rendered timeline top-to-bottom would see the 2014 study appear to follow the 2017 tragedy rather than precede it by three years.
blocking.evidence: timeline entries: {"year": 2017, "month": 12, ...} appears at array index 7, {"year": 2014, ...} appears at index 8, in showcase.json's timeline list.
blocking.fix: Reorder the timeline array so the 2014 "Feasibility study weighs jetty's fate" entry comes immediately before the 2017-12 "Father and son drown off Goat Rock Beach" entry (i.e., ...1985, 2003, 2014, 2017-12, 2018-5).

advisory.claim: "...and where swimmers drowned for decades before a lifeguard tower arrived."
advisory.problem: The sourced drowning record runs 2003-2017 (14 years), i.e. one decade plus four years, not the multiple full decades "decades" (plural) implies.
advisory.evidence: F35 (2003), F34 (2015), F33 (2016), F32 (2017) are the only dated drownings on the sheet; earliest is 2003, 15 years before the page's researched_at date.
advisory.fix: Change "drowned for decades" to "drowned for years" (or "for well over a decade").

advisory.claim: "...crews detonate 14 tons of black powder and dynamite..."
advisory.problem: F05's quote says only "14 tons of powder and dynamite" -- "black" is an added material specifier not present in the source.
advisory.evidence: F05 quote: "on nov. 17, 1929, thousands of spectators came to watch as 14 tons of powder and dynamite carved a crater in goat rock..."
advisory.fix: Remove "black": change to "14 tons of powder and dynamite" in both history.mdx and the showcase.json timeline description.

advisory.claim: "Goat Rock Beach was, by 2016, already one of the most-visited beaches in Sonoma County -- voters in a Metroactive readers' poll ranked it the county's second-most-popular beach."
advisory.problem: The Metroactive poll (F46) carries no date in the fact sheet; anchoring it to "by 2016" implies a confirmed timing the sheet doesn't support.
advisory.evidence: F46 has no date_of_source / year; cultural_refs entry for the poll lists year: null.
advisory.fix: Change "Goat Rock Beach was, by 2016, already one of the most-visited beaches in Sonoma County -- voters in a Metroactive readers' poll ranked it..." to "Goat Rock Beach was already, by all evidence, one of the most-visited beaches in Sonoma County -- voters in a Metroactive readers' poll ranked it..."
